## Root cause

This is a Type-C sysfs-link removal bug, not a Dell-specific kernfs failure.

The offending code is:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1195`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169-2186`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138-1154`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264-1364`

### Call chain from the warning

The UCSI work item processes a connector-change event:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264
        |
        +-- change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE
        |     drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1306
        |
        +-- disconnected state
              drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1324
                    |
                    +-- ucsi_unregister_partner()
                          drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138
                                |
                                +-- typec_unregister_partner()
                                      drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151
```

`ucsi_unregister_partner()` performs the partner teardown at `ucsi.c:1143-1153`, ultimately calling `typec_unregister_partner()` at line 1151.

`typec_unregister_partner()` then does:

```c
if (port->usb2_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
        port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
        port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1183-1191`.

The relevant helper is:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
                                        struct device *dev)
{
        sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
        sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

        if (partner->deattach)
                partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`.

The second removal is the one producing the warning:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");       /* class.c:909 */
```

## Why the same link is removed twice

The Type-C port installs this callback when the port is registered:

```c
port->con.deattach = typec_partner_deattach;
```

at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2751-2753`.

That callback is:

```c
static void typec_partner_deattach(struct typec_connector *con,
                                   struct device *dev)
{
        ...
        partner = typec_get_partner(port);
        if (partner) {
                typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);
                put_device(&partner->dev);
        }
        ...
}
```

at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169-2186`.

Therefore, the actual recursion is:

```text
typec_unregister_partner()
  class.c:1185 or :1189
    typec_partner_unlink_device()
      class.c:906
        sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, ...)
        sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")
          class.c:909
        partner->deattach(...)
          typec_partner_deattach()
            class.c:2177
              typec_partner_unlink_device()
                class.c:906
                  sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, ...)
                  sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")
                    class.c:909   <-- second removal
```

The first invocation removes the `typec` symlink. The `deattach` callback then invokes the same unlink helper again, so the second invocation attempts to remove a link which no longer exists.

`sysfs_remove_link()` eventually calls:

```text
sysfs_remove_link()
  fs/sysfs/symlink.c
    kernfs_remove_by_name()
      kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

The kernfs implementation is explicit:

```c
if (!parent) {
        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
             name);
        return -ENOENT;
}
```

at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1730-1734` in this tree.

For the normal “link does not exist” case, `kernfs_find_ns()` returns `NULL` at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:874-905`, and `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` returns `-ENOENT` at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1739-1752`.

Thus “no directory”/`ENOENT` is kernfs reporting that the parent/name being removed is no longer present in the expected sysfs hierarchy. In this case the practical cause is the duplicate removal of the `typec` link, not a missing Type-C port directory created by firmware.

## Is the fix present in this tree?

No.

The current tree still contains both sides of the recursion:

- `typec_partner_unlink_device()` removes the links and then calls `partner->deattach` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`.
- `typec_partner_deattach()` calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` again — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169-2179`.

So the fix is not present in the inspected source.

## Upstream fix

The upstream fix is the Type-C partner-link teardown fix which removes the recursive unlinking from `typec_partner_deattach()`/makes the detach path only update the cached USB-device pointers, leaving the actual sysfs-link removal to `typec_partner_unlink_device()`.

Conceptually, the corrected relationship is:

```text
typec_unregister_partner()
  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
       -> remove both sysfs links
       -> detach callback only clears state
```

and no longer:

```text
detach callback
  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
```

This is the upstream Type-C fix series commonly titled along the lines of:

> **USB: typec: Fix double removal of partner links**

It was posted as a small USB Type-C cleanup/fix series after the code in this 6.17-based tree and is not backported here. The affected files are:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`
- in some versions of the series, the associated Type-C core callback/link teardown code

The important fix is specifically to prevent `typec_partner_deattach()` from calling `typec_partner_unlink_device()` after that helper has already entered the detach callback. That eliminates the second call to:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:909`.

The warning is therefore fixed by the upstream Type-C partner-unlink/partner-detach series; it is not fixed by changing kernfs or by ignoring `-ENOENT`.
